svg.text: Power-bay carrier — wiring schematic (one carrier, every build, 2026-11-24)
Every harness by its CAD route ID (the yellow tags = the labels embossed on the carrier). Electrical view, not physical paths — the routing map is carrier_routing.png.

Transcribed from Power_Bay_Design.md §11.3.9 (harness table) — the DOC wins; check_figures_match_docs.py fails on any mismatch. EVERY BUILD (Ultra, Nova, Halo HV; Halo at its rebuild). Halo v1 as-built differs: rocker on the DROK branch, cover-mounted, no INA-B.
MAINS — down the +X side lane into the PSU terminal slot, ≥ 8 mm jacket-to-jacket from every LV run, 18 AWG silicone 600 V-rated
earth (green/yellow) = longest conductor; strain relief ≤ 50 mm from each end; snap-in forks + service loop
the PSU's own terminal cover stays — the carrier is NOT mains insulation;
barrier rib over the L/N/E third of the slot
CH2 BAT+/BAT- flying leads exit beside +V
ONE block per robot, every build
IN-A (V+) / IN-B (GND) — input faces the SHORT end
A1/B1 BUCK-IN A2/B2 TETHER-P A3/B3 FAN1-P
≥ 8 mm (3D) from the L/N/E screws; wires turn -X before the slot
A4/B4 FAN2-P A5/B5 MUS-IN A6 PHONE-IN+ B6 LAMP
creator: B6 = LAMP + PHONE-IN GND in ONE E1508
port map §11.3.3 · feed at the -X tower
pack - > CH2 BAT- DIRECT (never through INA-B's GND screw)
SIGNAL SIDE — the carrier's left (-X) lane; crosses power only at right angles
ONE 4-wire 26 AWG chain: G469 3 SDA / 5 SCL / 1 3V3 / 9 GND > INA-M > INA-B > TMP102 > INA3
INA-M is the single logic-to-power GND tie; INA3's and INA-B's GND screws stay EMPTY; pull-ups ~1.9-2.6 k (measure)
OUT > G469 36; 5V > pin 2, GND > pin 6 (4-in-1 ferrules, no Ys)
OUT > G469 11; 5V > pin 2, GND > pin 6 (4-in-1 ferrules, no Ys)
OUT > G469 38; 5V > pin 2, GND > pin 6 (4-in-1 ferrules, no Ys)
OUT > G469 40; 5V > pin 2, GND > pin 6 (4-in-1 ferrules, no Ys)
4x HC-SR501, fence corners > carrier corners > signal lane
RISERS through the servo-base opening above the G469: TETHER-P/-S, BUCK-OUT, USB-C go UP; SPS30/ZE15 come DOWN. FFC on the far side from the power pairs; edge protection where they bear.
